query: Help me understand what's worth analyzing in these travel-expense records.

per_column.name: asset_category
per_column.rationale: Categorizes the ci/short_description into asset types (hardware, cloud, travel, etc.), giving a solid grouping axis. Values track the source text well (Dell -> hardware_device, AWS EC2 -> cloud_service).

per_column.name: creation_mode
per_column.rationale: Derived from short_description phrasing ('Automated creation' -> automated_generation, 'Procurement' -> manual_procurement). Well grounded and offers a useful process-provenance axis, though somewhat descriptive-driven.

per_column.name: business_purpose
per_column.rationale: A useful grouping axis, but assignments are weakly grounded: 'Newly implemented cloud service' mapped to 'infrastructure_upgrade' and hardware assets uniformly to 'office_infrastructure' appear to be inferred labels not clearly warranted by the terse source text.

per_column.name: asset_specificity
per_column.rationale: Distinguishes named models vs generic references vs service abstractions from the ci field; well grounded (specific model strings -> named_model). Moderately useful but partly redundant with asset_category signal.

per_column.name: department_span
per_column.rationale: Largely redundant with the existing original 'department' column. The evidence rows offer no textual basis for the assigned department (customer_support/sales), suggesting values may not be reliably derivable from the shown source text.

per_column.name: processing_lag_signal
per_column.rationale: Bins the gap between opened_at and processed_date into same_day/multi_day/unknown; a genuinely useful operational axis and grounded (nan processed_date -> unknown_lag). Handles silence correctly.

per_column.name: source_tracking_completeness
per_column.rationale: A direct present/missing flag on the existing source_id column. Fully grounded but a near-trivial binary restatement of an original field, limiting analytical leverage.

per_column.name: asset_lifecycle_stage
per_column.rationale: Useful lifecycle grouping, but heavily skewed toward acquisition/registration and derivation is uneven (a row missing source_id mapped to 'registration' while similar 'addition' rows map to 'acquisition'), indicating some unwarranted inference.

judge.rationale: The added columns provide several genuine new axes for grouping travel/asset-expense records (asset_category, creation_mode, processing_lag_signal), which are both useful and reasonably grounded in ci/short_description/processed_date. Weaker columns are department_span (redundant with the original department column and poorly evidenced) and source_tracking_completeness (a trivial binary restatement). Groundedness is generally sound for extraction-style columns but drops for interpretive labels (business_purpose, asset_lifecycle_stage) where confident categories are asserted beyond what the terse source text supports.
